newsitem.title: ITALY: Financing operation starts for Italy's Ducati.
newsitem.headline: Financing operation starts for Italy's Ducati.

text.p: Paribas, Banca Commerciale Italiana (BCI) and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell are organising and underwriting financing for nearly 400 billion lire for Italian motorcycle group Ducati, a Paribas statement said.

Italian banks Banca Nazionale del Lavoro (BNL), Banca di Roma and Credito Italiano as well as Bank of America joined the operation before general syndication began, in the capacity of senior lead managers for 40 billion lire each.
The funds will be used for a relaunch programme which is expected to double Ducati production in the space of three years to 38,000 motorcycles by 1998 from 19,000 in 1996, a source at Ducati said.
"There's also the aim in two or three years of flotation possibly on Wall Street," the source said.
The financial plan envisages three levels of participation with 30 billion from lead managers, 20 billion from managers and 10 billion from participants.
Since September this year Ducati has been 49 percent controlled by the Castiglioni family and 51 percent by a group of investors led by Texas Pacific Group.
The two groups bought all the assets of Ducati from the Cagiva group which was itself owned by Castiglioni brothers.
